title: Inputs group — the eleven that bind $state
status: ACCEPTED — all eleven components rendered in a real DSH host, and V1–V5 verified there
verdict: ACCEPTED. browserRuns.claim: All eleven components render from one real program in the host
IME composition in a bound Input does not drop characters or disturb the pre-edit
browserRuns.method: Genuine composition mode through CDP Input.imeSetComposition, not a synthetic CompositionEvent — the page recorded 7 composition events and 5 input events carrying isComposing=true, which is what proves the browser really entered composition.
browserRuns.measured: Pre-edit advanced start → startn → startni → startnih → startnihao with no step dropped or reordered; caret advanced monotonically 5→6→7→8→10; focus never left the field; the node was never replaced; the commit 你好 landed once and reached $state (sibling Text read T=start你好); the other bound field stayed at n0.
browserRuns.note: The design does write $state on each input, pre-edit included. That is recorded, not defended: it is a defect only if it disturbs the composition, and the six assertions above measure exactly that. It did not.

browserRuns.claim: A ticking Timer beside a focused Input does not steal focus, reset the caret, or swallow input
browserRuns.measured: The timer really ticked: 8 distinct values 01:00 → 00:53 across the run. Six characters typed one real key event at a time across those ticks: all six landed in order, focus never left the field, the input node was never replaced, the caret advanced 1→2→3→4→5→6 and ended at the end of the text, and $state read N=ABCDEF.

observations.summary: The 4A-3 unit spec drives renderProgram directly, so it never exercises the name check
observations.detail: tests/openui-inputs-4a3.spec.tsx calls renderProgram(source, {}) from src/client/OpenUICard.tsx, which is drawProgram without the backend's checkNames pass. The spec therefore accepts Action([@Set($v, 1)]) as an IconButton action, while the live path rejects it with VZO002 'unknown component "Action"' — verified against the real validator. A model following the skill text never writes that form (languageReference() documents a bare @Set($v, value) step), so this is a fidelity gap in the test, not a live defect.
observations.impact: None on the product. It does mean the jsdom suite is slightly more permissive than the host, which is worth knowing before trusting a green spec as a statement about what a program may contain.
observations.status: Recorded, not fixed — changing the fixtures to the documented form is a test-only edit, and it is out of the minimal-change scope this acceptance run was given. It belongs in the 4A-4 test batch.

openQuestions.topic: The persisted meta stores the fragment twice
openQuestions.detail: presentationMeta writes both fragment and the pre-fork source; for a html card nothing reads source, so it is 234 bytes a card of dead payload.
openQuestions.whyNotFixedHere: removing it changes the persisted shape and needs an ADR
